Conversely, outcomes below the lower bounds could result from severe economic downturns, unexpected negative policy changes, escalating geopolitical crises, company-specific scandals or failures, or a widespread loss of investor confidence. These high-impact, low-probability events, often referred to as "black swans," are inherently difficult to quantify but represent scenarios that could lead to outcomes significantly outside the predicted ranges.
